narrative.text: Full text, Figure 1, acknowledgements, author affiliations, and references of the April 2021 Lancet Digital Health Comment 'WHO SMART guidelines: optimising country-level use of guideline recommendations in the digital age' by Garrett Mehl, Özge Tunçalp, Natschja Ratanaprayul, Tigest Tamrat, María Barreix, David Lowrance, Kidist Bartolomeos, Lale Say, Nenad Kostanjsek, Robert Jakob, John Grove, Bernardo Mariano Jr, and Soumya Swaminathan (Lancet Digit Health 2021; 3: e213–16). Explains how unsystematic, hard-coded translation of WHO guidelines into digital tools hinders interoperability, traceability, and updates, and introduces WHO's software-neutral SMART guidelines framework (Standards-based, Machine-readable, Adaptive, Requirements-based, and Testable) structured across five knowledge layers—L1 Narrative (enhanced living guidelines, adaptation toolkits, monitoring frameworks), L2 Operational (Digital Adaptation Kits [DAKs] defining personas, workflows, ICD/terminology-mapped data elements, decision support, and indicators), L3 Machine-readable (HL7 FHIR Implementation Guides and Clinical Quality Language [CQL] logic), L4 Executable (reference applications such as the WHO Digital ANC module, terminology services, SDKs, and APIs), and L5 Dynamic (precision health models trained on anonymised datasets)—illustrated using the WHO antenatal care (ANC) guideline test case.

Publication header metadata from page e213 of The Lancet Digital Health (Volume 3, April 2021, published online February 17, 2021; DOI 10.1016/S2589-7500(21)00038-8) for the Comment article introducing WHO SMART guidelines.
